title: Apply to enrol in the NSW international student program (secondary school)
summary: This page provides information on how international students can apply to enrol in a secondary school through the NSW international student program.
intro:
Qualifications from NSW government secondary schools (high schools) are recognised world wide, and the international student program caters for international students in more than 150 high schools in Sydney and regional locations.

High school begins in Year 7 (12 years of age) and ends in Year 12 (18 years of age). Subjects and activities covered include English, mathematics, science, technology, languages, creative arts and humanities.

If you successfully complete Year 12, you're awarded a Higher School Certificate (HSC) and Australian Tertiary Admissions Rank (ATAR).

Class sizes are usually between 10 and 30 pupils, and schools are equipped with libraries, auditoriums, gymnasiums, computer rooms and science laboratories.

If you're applying for a student visa and would like to enrol as an international student in a NSW secondary school, you'll need to complete an application form.
who_can_apply: For Years 7 and 8: You must live with a parent or a direct relative approved by the Department of Immigration and Border Protection, and achieve a minimum score of 5.0 in IELTS or an equivalent approved English language test, or have good grades in main academic subjects.

For Years 9 and 10: You may live with a parent, an approved direct relative, a parent-nominated carer, or a homestay family approved by the Department of Education International (DE International). You must achieve a minimum score of 5.5 in IELTS or an equivalent approved English language test, or have completed Year 10 or its equivalent in Australia or overseas, and have good passing grades in main academic subjects.
For junior high school (Year 7 to Year 10) and senior high school (Years 11 and 12): Specific eligibility criteria apply for each stage.
If you need help with your application, DE International has a worldwide network of representative agents.
what_you_need: Certified copy of your birth certificate or your passport.
Overseas student health cover (OSHC) details (if applicable).
Certified copies of your school reports for the last 2 years.
Evidence of English proficiency, such as:
Certified translations of all supporting documents that are not in English.

how_to_steps.text: Complete and submit your online application.

more_info.text: If you're talented in performing arts (dance, drama or music), technology, languages or sport, you can apply to high schools which offer specialist facilities.
Boys-only secondary high schools, girls-only secondary high schools, or co-educational secondary high schools (boys and girls) are available for international students.
If you need to improve your English skills before you enrol, you can apply for an intensive English language course.
High school applicants for Years 7-10 can enrol from Term 1 to Term 4.

Senior high school applicants for Year 11 must enrol in Term 1 or Term 2 only. It is best to enrol in Year 11 in January to ensure you have the most amount of time to learn the Preliminary HSC curriculum.

faqs.q: What qualifications are awarded upon completion of Year 12?
faqs.a: If you successfully complete Year 12, you are awarded a Higher School Certificate (HSC) and Australian Tertiary Admissions Rank (ATAR).

faqs.q: What are the typical class sizes and facilities at the schools?
faqs.a: Class sizes are usually between 10 and 30 pupils, and schools are equipped with libraries, auditoriums, gymnasiums, computer rooms, and science laboratories.

faqs.q: Who can apply for the program?
faqs.a: Eligibility depends on the year level (Years 7-10 or Years 11-12) and requires meeting specific criteria regarding English proficiency, academic grades, and living arrangements.
